assertion_audit.failure_conditions: Nonzero remaining count fails the checker result assertion; disabling chmod makes the redirect return zero and fails line 83 (recorded), missing permission refusal text fails line 84, truncation/content or mtime change fails line 85, retained write bits fail line 86, loss of executable behavior fails line 94, missing/duplicate repairs fail the count assertion, wrong target reporting fails the path inclusion/exclusion assertions, missing timestamp format fails the final assertion. Identity is independently sampled before mutation; executable output is a fixed decoy marker.

A redirect that is refused despite the disabled checker fails its return-code assertion; a missing/different write fails the replacement byte assertion; a decoy retaining its prior size/mtime/digest fails the changed-identity assertion. This is the positive overwrite control, not evidence of the enabled guard.

Linking the wrong environment fails the resolved-link assertion; a wrong receipt fails the linked-path assertion; removing the provisioning checker leaves write bits and permits redirect, failing two independent filesystem assertions; stdout repair chatter fails the empty-stdout assertion and absent/wrong stderr target fails the final assertion. The receipt path expectation uses a known fixture path and is corroborated by link identity and the refused redirect.

Restoring either consumer to its inline repo/.venv resolution fails the comparison to selected because selected belongs to the other decoy; bypassing the resolver in interpreter discovery fails its target tuple; no resolver invocation or resolving another repository fails the calls assertion. The monkeypatch is a dependency-substitution control: both consumers must observe an independently chosen alternative environment, so the assertion does not survive reinstating the bypass.

Including python-config/directories/dangling aliases or duplicate target entries fails the target tuple; reporting a false repair failure fails the zero result; sealing python-config fails its retained-write-bit assertion.

Swallowing chmod refusal as success fails count==1; omitting or misidentifying the failure fails the report assertion; removing the provisioning remaining-count refusal fails pytest.raises; exposing a link after failed repair fails the absent-link assertion.

Sampler failure fails its exit assertion; skipping a sample fails the three-row assertion; missing/renamed column fails the header assertion; missing/incorrect readings fail the two-zero assertion; omitting sealing on either pass leaves writable targets, successful redirects or damaged executables and fails those three assertions; missing/extra repairs or incorrect target names fail stderr count and path assertions. A later writable installation created between passes is a positive discovery control for the reported zero.
Stopping the sampler on registry failure fails returncode==0; returning healthy zero instead of unknown fails the final-column assertion; silently losing the diagnostic fails the stderr assertion.
Dropping or moving the appended writable_interpreters column fails the literal expected header comparison; the expected string is independent of sampler output.

Either from reckon.flight import ... or import reckon.flight reinstated in the script fails the AST allowlist; both mutations are recorded failing in assertion-import-control-from.log and assertion-import-control-direct.log. The expected allowed module is a fixed literal, not derived from inspected imports.
